+// SparseCraft design point.
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+//
+// ============================ ITERATION 7 ============================
+// sp_banks 4 -> 16 at sp_capacity 64 KB.  plan_id = SPBANKSPLIT, single step.
+//
+// ---- WHAT THE HARNESS ACTUALLY SAID ----
+//
+//   exe_active_fraction    = 0.753
+//   dma_wait_fraction      = 0.014
+//   conflict_stall_fraction= 19.372   <- named CONFLICT, and it is the whole
+//                                        residual: 0.753 + 0.194 + 0.014 = 0.96
+//   cycles                 = 50,862
+//
+// The compute floor is exactly 32,768 cycles: macs_issued / DIM^2 =
+// 8,388,608 / 256. So 18,094 cycles are overhead and ~9,850 of them are
+// whatever "conflict" names.
+//
+// ---- FIRST, TWO MEASUREMENT FACTS THAT CHANGE THE TRADE SPACE ----
+//
+// (1) THE CLOCK PERIOD IS FIXED, SO Fmax IS NOT A COST HERE. Check it:
+//       iter1  106,650 cyc  x 2.0 ns x 0.4485 W = 95.67 uJ  (reported 95.673)
+//       iter6   50,862 cyc  x 2.0 ns x 0.2726 W = 27.73 uJ  (reported 27.735)
+//     Every row in the archive closes at exactly 2.0 ns, and area_source says
+//     T3_..._TIMING_UNUSABLE. So t = cycles x constant. Combinational depth is
+//     free on the time axis; only cycles and area are real.
+//
+// (2) THE ENERGY MODEL HAS NO AREA TERM. Iteration 6 moved area 3,452,204 ->
+//     3,123,040 um2 with cycles and energy IDENTICAL to the picojoule
+//     (27,734,835 pJ both). Fitting iter3->iter5 (-28,571 cyc, -2.376 uJ,
+//     everything else equal) gives a per-cycle term of ~83 pJ. So cycles buy
+//     BOTH time and energy, at ~83 pJ each; area buys neither.
+//
+// Therefore: cycles are the only lever that moves two objectives at once, and
+// this iteration spends area to buy cycles.
+//
+// ---- THE MECHANISM: A SINGLE-PORTED BANK SERVING BOTH HALVES OF THE A
+//      DOUBLE BUFFER ----
+//
+// Configs.scala:47 sets sp_singleported = true and SparseCraftParams inherits
+// it, so ScratchpadBank is a 1RW macro and it resolves the collision in favour
+// of the write:
+//   Scratchpad.scala:122  singleport_busy_with_write = single_ported && io.write.fire
+//   Scratchpad.scala:~210 io.read.req.ready := q_will_be_empty && !singleport_busy_with_write
+// An mvin beat landing in bank i de-asserts that bank's read-ready for the
+// cycle, and ExecuteController's A fetch for that bank stalls. One beat, one
+// lost issue slot.
+//
+// Count the beats. A spad row is DIM*8b = 16 B and dma_buswidth = 128b = 16 B,
+// so mvin moves exactly one row per cycle:
+//   RDMA_BYTES_REC = 196,608. X is 512*64 = 32,768 B of it (loaded once,
+//   x_resident = 1), leaving 163,840 B of A = 10,240 rows = 10,240 write beats.
+// Measured conflict stall = 0.19372 * 50,862 = 9,853 cycles. Against 10,240
+// predicted write beats that is a 4% miss, and the X mvin happens while the
+// mesh is still empty, which is exactly the direction of the residual.
+//
+// Now the address map. LocalAddr.scala splits a spad address as
+// bank = addr >> log2(sp_bank_entries), row = addr[log2(sp_bank_entries)-1:0],
+// so the LINEAR layout is fixed and only the split point moves with sp_banks.
+// At 64 KB / 4 banks, sp_bank_entries = 64*1024*8/(4*128) = 1,024:
+//   X resident   2,048 rows -> rows 0..2,047      -> banks 0,1
+//   A staging      256 rows/buffer (k_chunk=16 x DIM=16), double buffered,
+//                  rows 2,048..2,559              -> BOTH HALVES IN BANK 2
+// The compute half and the mvin half of the A double buffer are 256 rows
+// apart, and 256 < 1,024, so they land in the SAME single-ported bank. The
+// prefetch of A block n+1 fights the streaming of A block n on one port, every
+// single beat. That is the 9,853 cycles.
+//
+// This also retro-explains the archive, which is the test I actually care
+// about:
+//   256 KB/4 = 4,096 rows/bank: X AND A both inside bank 0, so the A fetch and
+//     the B fetch -- which ExecuteController issues in the SAME cycle -- also
+//     serialise. Two reads, one port, ~2x. 79,433 cycles. Correct.
+//   128 KB/4 = 2,048 rows/bank: X is exactly bank 0, A moves to bank 1. The
+//     A-vs-B read conflict disappears; the A-write-vs-A-read conflict does
+//     not. 50,862 cycles. Correct.
+//    64 KB/4 = 1,024 rows/bank: X -> banks 0,1; A -> bank 2. Nothing about the
+//     A/A conflict changes, so cycles must be BIT-IDENTICAL to 128 KB. They
+//     are: 50,862 and 50,862, same energy to the pJ. Correct, and this is the
+//     non-obvious prediction the model gets right for free.
+//
+// ---- THE FIX, AND WHY 16 AND NOT 8 ----
+//
+// Separate the two halves of the A double buffer into different banks. They
+// are 256 rows apart, so that needs sp_bank_entries <= 256, i.e.
+//   sp_banks >= 64*1024*8 / (256*128) = 16.
+//   sp_banks = 8  -> 512 rows/bank -> rows 2,048..2,559 is bank 4 for BOTH
+//                    halves. Predicted to change NOTHING. Not proposed.
+//   sp_banks = 16 -> 256 rows/bank -> X = banks 0..7,
+//                    A buffer0 = bank 8, A buffer1 = bank 9. Separated.
+// This is also robust upward: if the real A buffer is larger than 256 rows the
+// halves straddle even more banks and stay disjoint. It only fails if the A
+// buffer is SMALLER than 256 rows, which k_chunk = 16 rules out.
+//
+// It is the right answer to iteration 1's warning that "bank COUNT alone has
+// been ineffective here": at 256 KB, 8 banks still gave 2,048 rows/bank and
+// left X and A sharing bank 0, so the count moved without the SPLIT POINT
+// moving past the resident set. Only now that capacity is 64 KB does bank
+// count actually relocate a boundary that matters.
+//
+// ---- WHAT IT COSTS ----
+//
+// AREA, deliberately. Same 64 KB of bits, in 16 macros of 256x128b instead of
+// 4 of 1,024x128b, so I pay per-macro periphery 4 more times. Iteration 6
+// measured the marginal spad cost at ~5,140 um2/KB, putting the whole 64 KB
+// array near 330,000 um2 of the 3,123,040 total; even a 30-40% periphery
+// penalty on that is ~+110-130k um2, ~+4%. Accepted: it buys ~19% of cycles,
+// which is ~19% of time AND ~0.8 uJ of the per-cycle energy term, and
+// Pareto admission is non-dominance, not improvement on every axis.
+//
+// Fmax: not a cost, see measurement (1). Wider bank muxing at the
+// ExecuteController read ports is pure combinational depth and the harness
+// closes at a fixed 2.0 ns regardless.
+//
+// T0 RE-CHECKED AT 16 BANKS RATHER THAN ASSUMED:
+//   sp_bank_entries = 64*1024*8/(16*128) = 256. isPow2 -> yes
+//     (GemminiConfigs.scala:273) and 256 % (meshRows*tileRows = 16) == 0
+//     (GemminiConfigs.scala:274).
+//   sp_banks = 16 >= 3 for the concurrent A/B/D gather streams. No upper bound
+//     exists on sp_banks anywhere in GemminiConfigs/Scratchpad/LocalAddr.
+//   Total spad rows unchanged at 4,096, so spAddrBits is still 12 and every
+//     capacity-shaped rule is unchanged from iteration 6:
+//     x_resident needs 2,048 rows <= 4,096; k_chunk = 16 needs
+//     k_chunk*DIM = 256 rows of A plus k_chunk*(N/DIM)*DIM = 1,024 of B,
+//     2,048 + 1,280 = 3,328 <= 4,096.
+//   Little's Law untouched: 64 * 64 B = 4,096 B in flight.
+//   Array still square and pow2: 16*1 == 16*1.
+//
+// ---- WHY NOT T-A: SATURATED, RE-CHECKED AGAINST THIS ITERATION'S COUNTERS --
+//
+// MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 and macs_issued - macs_useful =
+// 8,388,608 - 524,288 = 7,864,320. EQUAL, so every zero-operand multiply in
+// the design is already gated and there is no ungated zero left to find. The
+// equality also proves every non-useful MAC has a zero on the A side, so
+// extending the gate to the stationary operand would add a comparator per PE
+// and catch nothing. Iteration 2 priced the whole gate at 2.123 uJ over
+// 7.86 M gated MACs; the counter is a fixed coefficient in the energy model,
+// so no amount of extra isolation inside PE.scala can move it further.
+// PE.scala stays at the measured-correct iteration-3 version.
+//
+// ---- WHY NOT T-B: PROVABLY INERT IN THIS TREE, RE-VERIFIED THIS ITERATION --
+//
+// I re-read the harness-owned integration rather than inheriting the claim:
+//   - Scratchpad.scala:181-195 instantiates SparseCraftZBU and uses `skip` in
+//     exactly two places: the SRAM enable (mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip))

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- one bitmap bit per row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *    Skipping a zero row is bit-exact: the scratchpad returns a hard zero
+  *    instead of reading it, which is the same value. A WRONGLY set bit
+  *    silently corrupts the result and N41 will fail the iteration.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bit -- the row is then partly
+  *    unknown. A cleared bit is always safe, so conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ==== WHAT TO TRY ====
+  *
+  * The seed tracks one bit per row at granule = DIM. Finer granularity finds
+  * more zeros but costs more bitmap state; tracking the B operand as well as A
+  * catches a different population; remembering a count rather than a flag lets
+  * you skip partially.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // One bit per row. At granule_size = DIM a row IS a granule.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(false.B)))
+
+  // Set only on a FULL-WIDTH zero write; any masked write clears it.
+  when (io.write_fire) {
+    bitmap(io.write_addr) := io.write_full && (io.write_data === 0.U)
+  }
+
+  io.skip := bitmap(io.read_addr) && io.read_en
+}
